findings.title: Existing recreate-upgrade exit code silently changed from 4 to 3
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3 and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script or pipeline that already treats exit code 4 as "recreate required" will now read 4 as "feature disabled" and 3 as recreate. The documented meaning of the codes changes in place. The guide also still describes this tool as an evolving preview, but anything that already consumed the old code is broken without notice. Consumers inside the repo, such as the Operator code that runs the check, must be audited and updated. This diff does not touch any.

findings.title: Feature check runs before option/config validation and relies on early profile init
findings.body: `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` is called first in run(). `Profile.getInstance()` may be null if the profile is not yet configured, which would throw an NPE. Also, `--features=rolling-updates` is a build-time option. When the server is run with `--optimized` (a mixin is present on these commands), a feature that was not enabled at build time is not picked up. The same applies to the identical check in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata. The only behaviour tested is the non-optimized dist case.

findings.title: Feature-disabled test does not check exit code and covers only the metadata command
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message for the `metadata` subcommand. It does not assert exit code 4, which is the new contract that scripts rely on and is documented. It also never exercises `check` with the feature disabled. A regression in the `check` path, or in the exit code, would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Appended --features flag is placed after user parameters in every generated example
findings.body: The macro appends `--features=rolling-updates` after `${parameters}` in all generated update-compatibility examples. The guide text then tells users to supply the same options as for `start`, but the example hides the fact that the feature is required. Only the CAUTION block mentions it. Users copying only the snippet get the flag, but anyone writing their own command lines or config files has to find the CAUTION block. The `--features` value also replaces rather than adds to the user's feature list when they already pass `--features`, and the docs do not warn about this.
